items.mnemonic: Into the face of a CLIFF, THREE ledges have been hacked out with a blunt WEAPON, one above the other — each ledge is a STEP.
A TREE has toppled and lies flat, its YELLOW autumn leaves spread along the ground — it no longer points up but to the SIDE.
WATER pours into a HOLE so far down that a whole TREE could stand in it unseen — it is that DEEP.
A bolt of LIGHTNING splits the sky, and you drop your voice to a bow and SAY HUMBLY what you came to report.
Carved into a TREE is a SHEEP standing over flowing WATER — the family crest that tells you the MANNER in which this house does everything.
A SHELL, the oldest kind of coin, placed in the hand of true TALENT — that is how a family builds its WEALTH.
WATER laps at a pier where TWENTY boats tie up EIGHT deep, their ropes coiled like a SNAKE on the stones — this is the HARBOR.
To SAY a thing, to hear its SOUND, and to test it on the edge of a HALBERD — only then can you claim to truly KNOW it.
A MOUTH opens wide, two HORNS of breath shoot out and curl into a HOOK that catches a friend across the street — that is how you CALL someone.
Down the ROAD, over hard-packed EARTH, a SHEEP trots steadily on until at last it is at the pen — to REACH the goal.
One DROP of sweet sauce on top of a STUBBORN old pot of stew — and suddenly the whole thing tastes GOOD.
On a HILL a CLIFF drops away, and you steady yourself with your RIGHT HAND on the rock as you pick your way down the SLOPE.
A MARQUIS steps outside and draws one STROKE across his almanac for every cloud he counts — his daily record of the WEATHER.
A bundle of GRAIN is held up to the MOUTH of the KING: he bites once and judges exactly how ripe it is — the EXTENT of the harvest.
WATER rises through the GRASS on BOTH banks until the field can hold not one drop more — the pond is FULL.
The merchant's last SHELL coin bounces off the table at the STRIKE of the auction gavel — the bid is lost, the deal a DEFEAT.
A PERSON looks TEN times with a sharp EYE before casting a FISHHOOK for the catch — judging whether it is worth the PRICE.
Out of a HOLE in the ground shoots something BIG, all at once — a THRUST that nobody saw coming.
Your FOOT follows the WALKING LEGS of a thousand travelers before you, down to the MOUTH of the valley — a well-trodden ROAD.
Every kind of GRAIN is measured with the same LADLE and poured into its own bin — each bin a separate DEPARTMENT.
Sack after sack of GRAIN, each grown from one tiny SPROUT, is stacked beside the SHELL money paid for it — the harvest you PILE UP.
A PERSON keeps a wary eye on a SCORPION crossing the path — it belongs to another world, it is something OTHER.
WALKING LEGS carry a pile of paperwork to the TABLE, where every sheet is sorted and settled — the place where you DEAL WITH things.
Under your ROOF, WALKING LEGS stop at the threshold and a MOUTH offers a polite greeting — a GUEST has arrived.
A NEGATIVE sign hangs above a MOUTH that stays firmly shut — the answer is to DENY.
On a HEAP of practice pieces sits ONE perfect square of CLOTH, dyed without a flaw — the work of the TEACHER everyone studies under.
You pitch a TENT on the summit and open a tin of BEAN soup to celebrate — the reward for the long CLIMB.
Under the SUN a bright FLAG flaps in a warm wind, and the whole day feels EASY.
Down the ROAD rolls a tightly bound SHEAF of wheat, bouncing quicker and quicker toward the mill — that is FAST.
A TALENT for drawing shows in a CHILD before anyone teaches it — the gift was already there; it does EXIST.
Two wings beat up and away, the long neck stretched forward — the whole character is a crane caught in mid-FLY.
An X-shaped CROSS is scratched into the bark of a sick TREE, and the forester raises a WEAPON to cut the blight down and KILL it before it spreads.
A MOUTH shouts a name, and the sound bends down into a HOOK that snags one ticket from the pile — your NUMBER is called.
Two HORNS of grass stick up from a single RICE FIELD, and TEN furrows run straight down it — nothing else, just SIMPLE.
Under a LEAN-TO, one PERSON and then another PERSON settle onto the bare EARTH to rest their legs — to SIT.
A STONE is hurled at a drum of stretched SKIN and rips straight through it — to BREAK.
On the HILL a PERSON sweeps ONE SMALL pile of dead leaves off the path and over the edge — to REMOVE it.
The ROOF is on, the TWO beams are set, and the LEGS of the frame stand true — the house is COMPLETE.
Down the HILL come WALKING LEGS, hurrying as the first rain hits the CLOTHESLINE below — time to DESCEND and bring the laundry in.
The single SPROUT you promised to water has withered, and the SHELL coins you were paid lie untouched — the BLAME is yours.
A HAND darts into the SEEDBED and closes around the rabbit nibbling the shoots — to CATCH.
A parcel BOUND UP with string teeters on the edge of a CLIFF, held only by a wax SEAL that is starting to crack — DANGEROUS.
A spool of THREAD is handed to each PERSON, ONE for every MOUTH they have to feed, at the end of the week — the SUPPLY of wages.
GRASS so old it has sat TEN years in the jar — one leaf on the tongue makes your MOUTH twist, and you SUFFER the bitterness.
You hurry down the ROAD and find a RABBIT already sitting at the gate, ears up, waiting to WELCOME you home.
An EYE inspects ONE box with EIGHT compartments, each holding a hammer, a chisel, a plane — every TOOL in its place.
Your TONGUE burns on something SPICY, and the words that come out are your farewell — you RESIGN on the spot.
Inside a square ENCLOSURE lies something BIG, the one thing that explains everything else in the room — the CAUSE.
A CLAW gently lifts the COVER off a HEART, and WALKING LEGS carry it carefully to the one who needs it — that is LOVE.
Under one ROOF stands a WINE JUG so full it never runs dry — the sign of real WEALTH.
A STEP sounds behind you, and you know that coat of worn leather SKIN before you even turn — it is HE.
A young tree whose top branch is still shorter than the one below it: it has NOT YET grown into its full height.
Out of NOTHINGNESS a pair of DANCING LEGS appears on the empty stage and begins to turn — the DANCE has started.
A lid with one leg broken away, the simple old sign of the DECEASED: what once stood here has gone — to DIE and be no more.
ICE crackles as a PERSON pecks ONE hole in it with a BEAK-shaped pick and dips a hand in — COLD to the bone.
By the ROAD you STAND a wooden FRAME, try TEN hats on it, and every MOUTH in the crowd calls out the one that fits — SUITABLE.
At the wedding a WOMAN is handed a BROOM, a COVER and a CLOTH as symbolic gifts for the new household — the old sign for WIFE.
Under a ROOF, a BIG hat hangs on one NAIL by the door, and a MOUTH calls out to come in — you APPROACH and stop by for a while.
On a narrow ROAD everyone tries to ENTER the same tiny shop at once — CROWDED.
Grains of RICE are sorted by a BIG HEAD that nods at each one — long, short, sticky — every grain to its own KIND.
A PERSON finishes dinner and ONE SMALL dumpling is still sitting on the plate — the SURPLUS nobody could eat.
TEN hairpins fanned out like a BROOM crown the hair of a WOMAN on her wedding morning — WIFE.
Two people stand NORTH to south, facing away from each other under the MOON, so each sees only the other's BACK.
EARTH piled on EARTH, EIGHT logs stacked in a ROUND mound, and a FIRE lit beneath it all — the kiln glows with HEAT.
Under one ROOF a PERSON lies down among a HUNDRED mats laid out for travelers — a night's LODGING.
A HILL so sharp it looks like an AWL point stabbing the sky — the path up it is STEEP.
You carry a heavy SHEAF to the neighbor's door and bow your HEAD: could you thresh this for me? — a REQUEST.
SMALL sparks fly from under a COVER; you lift it and SEE the glowing page you studied last night — now you REMEMBER.
On the ROAD a PERSON stops at ONE SMALL teahouse halfway to the next town — the WAY is long and you are in the middle of it.
You SAY your apology at NOON, when the sun is highest and hides nothing — and the answer is yes, they PERMIT it.
One HAND grips the weed, the whole ARM leans back, and your RIGHT HAND gives the final tug to EXTRACT it, root and all.
A RABBIT sits in the middle of the RICE FIELD and will not budge however loudly you clap — it means to STAY.
A NET drops over whoever did WRONG, and the whole village sees it — a CRIME.
A WOMAN plants her RIGHT HAND on the millstone and turns it with all her POWER — pure EFFORT.
RICE polished until it gleams BLUE-white in the morning light — every husk gone, only the pure SPIRIT of the grain left.
TWENTY petals glow under the MOON until one STRIKE of wind sends them whirling across the garden — to SCATTER.
A BLUE pond, the wind BOUND UP and put away, a BROOM resting on its HOOK by the door — nothing stirs; everything is QUIET.
A WOMAN joins a new CLAN as the SUN goes down and the lanterns are lit for the evening feast — the ceremony of MARRIAGE.
A DRUM pounds in the square and every MOUTH breaks into song — to REJOICE.
On the WATER a CLAW-shaped hook holds a CHILD's paper boat so it bobs but never sinks — it will FLOAT.
A THREAD, BOUND UP tight around a COIL, is snipped with one clean cut — CUT OFF for good.
A hairpin with a bright head stuck upright in the earth where a gift lies buried: the simple old sign for HAPPINESS.
A HAND flat against a plate of ARMOR, shoving with all its weight until the plate gives — to PUSH.
A PERSON hurries to ARRIVE before the storm, and a SWORD of wind snaps the signpost in two — the first thing to FALL OVER.
BAMBOO stalks cut at the TEMPLE for writing slips, every one trimmed to exactly the same length — EQUAL.
Long hair, a bent back and a cane: the OLD figure walking home at dusk, the very picture of OLD AGE.
One STEP, then another, while the others RUN past on horseback — you go ON FOOT.
